title: Pattern catalog entry
description: One design pattern and the roles its participants can hold. A pattern whose single role carries the pattern's own name is emitted as a flat attribute; every other pattern is emitted as a static container holding one attribute per role.

catalog.description: The body of work the pattern comes from. Becomes both the namespace and the Catalog property.

name.description: The pattern name, in PascalCase. Also names the file and the generated container.

summary.description: What the pattern is for, in one sentence. Becomes the XML documentation of the container.

inherited.description: Whether a derived type still holds the role. A semantic property of the pattern: true for the DDD markers, since a subtype of an Entity is an Entity; false for the GoF roles, since a subtype of a Component is not necessarily a Leaf.

roles.description: The roles a participant can hold. Order is preserved in the generated source.

reference.description: The work the pattern comes from. Load-bearing, not editorial: a pattern is held by every catalogue whose work presents it as its own (ADR-0028), and the reference is what says which work that is.

specialisationOf.description: The pattern this one narrows, which must be a pattern of the SAME catalogue. A relation is emitted as inheritance and each catalogue ships as its own package (ADR-0027), so a relation across catalogues cannot exist; the validator rejects one. Name a role of the target where the work says this pattern is a way of being that participant rather than a kind of the whole pattern (ADR-0034).

name.description: The role name, in PascalCase. Becomes both the attribute name and the RoleName value.

targets.description: What the role can be applied to. Method, Constructor, Property and Field are member roles; they are generated exactly like the others, only their target differs. Declare Struct wherever a record struct would be a legitimate participant.

repeatable.description: Whether one declaration can hold the role more than once. A type can play one role in two occurrences of a pattern, so a type role is usually repeatable; a member holds a member role once, and an assembly is one bounded context rather than several. Stated per role rather than derived from the targets, because it is a fact about the pattern (ADR-0009).

summary.description: What this participant does within the pattern, in one sentence. Becomes the XML documentation of the attribute, and is what a reader sees in IntelliSense when choosing a role.

links.description: Names of other roles of the same pattern this one can point at, each generated as an optional typed property. Use them only where the type hierarchy alone cannot tell which occurrence of the pattern is meant.

externalLinks.description: Types this role can point at that are NOT roles of the pattern, each generated as an optional typed property. Where a link names a participant of the same occurrence, use `links`; use this where the role has to name a type the pattern does not own — the single caller a member is restricted to, for one.

name.description: The property name, in PascalCase. Must not collide with a role of the pattern or with another link of the same role.

summary.description: What the type named by this property is, in one sentence. Becomes the XML documentation of the property.

role.description: The role of the target this pattern narrows, where what the work states is that this pattern is a way of being one participant rather than a kind of the whole pattern (ADR-0034). Omit it, and the relation is to the pattern: to its single attribute when the target is flat, to its abstract Role base otherwise. Naming a role of a flat target is rejected, since that relation is already attribute to attribute.
